close_reason: Added final build_first_valid_path call after AIA loop so last iteration's fetches are consulted before AiaDepthExceeded.
description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:597 `for _iteration in 0..AIA_MAX_DEPTH` runs build→fetch in that order. After the final iteration (iter=4), the loop adds fetched certs to the pool then exits without ever calling `build_first_valid_path` on the augmented pool, so the last fetch round's results are never consulted. AIA_MAX_DEPTH=5 documents '5 fetch iterations' but effectively yields 'fetch up to 5 times, build only 5 times against fetch outputs 0..4'. Trigger: a 5-deep AIA chain where each intermediate's caIssuers must be fetched in sequence — the 5th fetch lands in the pool, then AiaDepthExceeded is returned instead of the successful path that one more build attempt would have produced. Fix: after the loop, call build_first_valid_path one final time with the fully-augmented pool, OR restructure the loop so build runs after each successful fetch round (which is what the iteration semantics imply). The bead-stated default of 5 in the rustdoc would then mean '5 hops resolved' rather than '4 hops resolved'.
title: AIA_MAX_DEPTH off-by-one: last fetch is wasted
